p012.text: The stream emits an event on every pause-state transition.
A new subscriber immediately receives the current pause value (replay on subscribe).
p012.quote: replays the current value on subscribe.

p012.text: Calling pause or resume when already in that state (idempotent calls) does not emit again.
p012.quote: Idempotent [pause] and [resume] calls do not re-emit.

p012.text: A plain broadcast controller would give a new listener nothing until the next transition.
p012.quote:
A plain broadcast controller tells a new listener
nothing until the next transition.

p012.text: Without replay, a control mounted while speech is held would show 'not paused' over a held queue until someone toggles.
p012.quote:
A control mounted while speech is already held would then show
"not paused" over a held queue until somebody toggles.

p012.text: The hold is global and Quick Ask mounts its own controls, so subscribing mid-hold is the ordinary case.
p012.quote:
The hold is global and Quick Ask mounts its own controls, so
arriving mid-hold is the ordinary case.

p012.text: Consumers also seed their initial state from the synchronous isPaused getter via initialData, and this should be kept.
p012.quote: Consumers also seed from the synchronous [isPaused] getter through `initialData`. Keep that.

p012.text: initialData paints the first frame, while the replayed value arrives one microtask later.
p012.quote: `initialData` paints the first frame and the replay lands one microtask later.

p012.text: Dropping initialData would trade a silent wrong state for a one-frame flash.
p012.quote:
Dropping it trades
a silent wrong state for a one-frame flash.

p063.text: A posted Android notification carries a payload that allows a tap to be routed back to its message.
p063.quote: What a posted Android notification carries so a tap can be routed back to its message.

p063.text: The payload crosses a process boundary, so it must be treated as untrusted input when read back.
p063.quote: The payload crosses a process boundary, so it is untrusted input on the way back.

p063.text: The payload string may be written by the background isolate or by a build that is no longer installed.
p063.quote: The background isolate, or a build no longer installed, writes the string.

p063.text: Android stores the payload in the notification's intent.
p063.quote: Android stores it in the notification's intent

p063.text: The payload is read by a fresh main isolate, possibly days after it was written.
p063.quote: a fresh main isolate reads it, possibly days later.

p063.text: There is no guarantee that the payload's shape survives between writing and reading.
decode is total: it never throws, and returns null for any malformed, empty, legacy or truncated payload.
p063.quote:
[decode] is total: every malformed, empty, legacy or
truncated payload returns null instead of throwing.

p063.text: A tap whose payload cannot be decoded results in a plain app launch rather than a crash on the launch path.
p063.quote: A tap that cannot be decoded degrades to a plain app launch, never a crash on the launch path.

p068.text: One wake shows at most a capped number of the most unplayed items.
p068.quote: The most unplayed items one wake shows.

p068.text: The server wakes the app only when a new notification arrives.
p068.quote: The server wakes only for a new notification

p068.text: Without a cap, a backlog of unplayed items would sit unseen behind the first item until the app was opened.
p068.quote:
so a backlog would otherwise sit unseen behind the first item
until the app opened.

p068.text: The cap exists to stop a long backlog from flooding the notification shade.
p068.quote: The cap stops a long backlog flooding the shade

p068.text: The cap exists to stop a long backlog from outrunning the handler window.
Items beyond the cap remain unplayed after the wake.
p068.quote: Whatever is past the cap stays unplayed.

p068.text: The design rationale is recorded in src/docs/decisions/README.md under R-PUSH-drain-each.

p027.text: The value is a share (fraction) of the pane's width that a bubble may use, acting as a maximum width.
p027.quote: Share of the pane's width a bubble may use.

p027.text: Previously bubbles were capped at a fixed width of 320 px.
The fixed 320 px cap left bubbles at only about half the width of an unfolded Pixel Fold.
p027.quote: left bubbles at about half the width of an unfolded Pixel Fold.

p027.text: The header spanned the full width of the pane, which contrasted with the narrower bubbles.
p027.quote: The header spanned all of it

p027.text: The bubble cap now scales with the screen width instead of being a fixed pixel value.
p027.quote: so the cap now follows the screen.

p062.text: An event is emitted whenever the stop-list (gate 1) suppresses an item on the enqueueAlways path.
p062.quote: Emits whenever the stop-list (gate 1) suppresses an item on the [enqueueAlways] path.

p062.text: Suppression is made observable because an early return with no signal looks like a hang.
p062.quote: Suppression is observable: an early return with no signal looks like a hang.

p062.text: For a response_requested question, the server is blocked while the user hears and sees nothing if suppression is silent.
p062.quote:
For a `response_requested`
question the server is blocked while the user hears and sees nothing.

p062.text: The event carries the matched rule, so a caller can name it.
p062.quote:
The event carries the matched rule,
so a caller can name it.

p062.text: The event carries enough of the original call to re-issue it through speakAnyway.
p062.quote: It also carries enough of the original call to re-issue it through [speakAnyway].

p062.text: The event is not emitted on the legacy enqueueIfSpeakable path.
p062.quote: It is not emitted on the legacy [enqueueIfSpeakable] path.

p062.text: The legacy enqueueIfSpeakable path is pinned byte-identical.
The legacy path's production dispatch is withdrawn at the DI seam.
p062.quote:
its production
dispatch is withdrawn at the DI seam

p062.text: Nothing the user must act on arrives through the legacy path, which is why no event is emitted there.
p062.quote: nothing the user must act on arrives through it.

p070.text: The check returns true when the fraction is zero or less.
p070.quote: True when [fraction] is zero or less

p070.text: A slider set to 0% means silence, which is the reason for the rule.
The zero-silence rule is not exempted for the first sentence, a short message spoken whole, a title, or an answer the user asked for; all of these are silenced too.
p070.quote: It is not the first sentence, a short message spoken whole, a title or an answer the user asked for.

p070.text: Every speech path performs this check before it enqueues speech.
p070.quote: Every speech path checks this before it enqueues

p070.text: The background FCM speech path is also covered by this check.
The design rationale is documented in src/docs/decisions/README.md under R-TTS-zero-silence.
